increments.title: The shared brief carries the winning form
increments.goal: Audit every rule in skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md against the four rows of the form table and the ban on exemption clauses, rewrite the rules whose form loses without changing what any of them requires, and cover each rewrite with a test-repo.sh case that turns red when the rule is restored to its replaced wording. This is the page every agent runs under and the densest set of rules in the repository, so it goes first and settles how the audit is judged and how the verdict is recorded for the rest of the run.
criteria: Every rule on skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md is read against all four rows of the form table and against the ban on exemption clauses.
Every rule whose form loses against the failure it prevents is rewritten into the winning form, and no rewrite changes what the rule requires.
Any exemption clause bolted onto an existing rule on this page is re-cut into a rule keyed to an observable predicate, with each branch stated on its own.
Where the winning form cannot be written without changing what the rule requires, the rule is left as it stands and the conflict is returned as a question for the human.
Each rewritten rule has a case in test-repo.sh that turns red when that rule is restored to the wording it replaced.
The verdict is recorded rule by rule for this page, and every rule left unchanged carries the reason it needs no rewrite.
`bash test.sh` exits 0.

return.plan:
INC-01 rewrites nine rules on skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md into the form .claude/rules/authoring.md picks for the failure each prevents, and adds one section to test-repo.sh pinning every rewrite against the wording it replaced. No other file changes. Every rule on the page was read against all four table rows and the ban on patching a rule with an exemption; the rule-by-rule verdict is at the bottom of this field, and it is where criterion 6 is satisfied (the codemap forbids a new document for it).

== HARD CONSTRAINTS ON ANY EDIT TO THIS PAGE ==
test-repo.sh already greps this page in eighteen places, and three cases assert the brief is the ONLY page carrying a phrase. Keep all of this true:
(a) These strings must survive verbatim and contiguous once newlines collapse to single spaces: `push the commit`; `already committed`; `backlog.mjs`; `## The mutation standard`; `counts as tested`; `increment`; `user-visible behaviour`; `public contract`; `data model`; `dependency footprint`; `irreversible`; `decidable`; A material question goes in `questions`; `A non-empty list ends the run`; `A decidable one never does`; `pick the default`; record it in `rulings`; the bold `rulings` bullet; `one string naming the decision, the reason, and what it costs if the default is wrong`; `steering projection`.
(b) These must NOT appear anywhere on the page — each is owned by another page and guarded by an ownership case that fails the moment a second page carries it: occasion, rationalisation, exemption clause, chain depth, argus, OTEL_, UROBOROS_OBS, collector, handoff / hand-off (the heading "You do not hand over" is safe: the guard is the regex hand-?off), and the filenames researcher.md, test-author.md, implementer.md, reviewer.md, planner.md, backlog.md.
(c) Quote every excuse with straight double quotes, the way the existing line `— "`npm test -- src/api`, 104 cases, exit 0", never "green" alone.` already does. No apostrophes inside a quoted excuse — the test cases grep for them from single-quoted shell strings.

== THE NINE REWRITES ==
Line numbers are from the file as it stands at b97832a. Replace the whole passage named; keep the surrounding text untouched.

R1+R2 — lines 18-24, the whole `**Commit your step, then push it.**` paragraph. Failure class: a rule skipped under pressure (row 1). Old form: an instruction that named its price but neither prohibited the skip nor quoted the excuse; the default-branch sentence named no price at all. New text:

**Commit your step, then push it.** You commit your work where your page says
to, and you push that commit straight away. Never keep a commit local while you
carry on working — not "one push at the end will do", not "the container is
still up": an unpushed commit dies with the container that made it, and the run
state it carries dies with it. Retry a failed `git push` up to four times,
waiting 2s, 4s, 8s and 16s; a push that still fails is a line in your return's
summary, not a stopped step. Never push to the default branch and never open a
pull request — not "the work is done and the branch is green": the default
branch moves only through a pull request a human merges, opening it is your
caller's, and anything that reaches that branch another way is a change no
human approved.

What it requires is unchanged: commit where your page says, push straight away, retry four times with that backoff, report a still-failing push in the summary, never open the pull request. "Never push to the default branch" states what "moves only through a pull request a human merges" already required.

R3 — lines 30-34, the sentence beginning "Read exactly the steps and the fields". Failure class: row 1; the price was there, the prohibition and the excuse were not. New text:

Read exactly the steps and the fields your prompt names, with the helper
subcommand it gives you, and never read a step or a field it did not name — not
"it is in the same file anyway", not "one more field would save me a guess": a
field of another role's step that your prompt did not send you to is not yours,
and reading it is how a role that is meant to be independent stops being one.

R4 — lines 70-71, the Bash bullet. Failure class: behaviour that depends on a condition (row 4); "when one fits" is a judgement call that decides neither branch. New text:

- Use the tools above where one of them does the thing; use Bash where the
  thing needs a shell — a command to run, `git`, or the backlog helper.

What it requires is unchanged: a dedicated tool where one does the job, Bash for shell-only work. The predicate is now observable (is the thing one of the listed tools does) and both branches are stated.

R5 — lines 78-82, the closed-list paragraph. Failure class: row 1. Its branches were already keyed to a predicate and stay so; what it lacked was the price and the quoted excuse. New text:

Where your prompt lists the commands this change is judged by, that list is
closed: run exactly those and nothing else. Never run a suite, a linter or a
formatter the list does not name, and never go looking for a runner yourself —
not "the whole suite is right there", not "it is one more command": a run you
were not asked for costs the run its minutes and hands you a failure someone
else owns, which you then either report as yours or bury. An empty list means
you run nothing and say so.

R6 — lines 107-110, the shape of one ruling. Failure class: an omitted required element (row 3); the three parts were asked for in prose, with no slot that makes a missing one visible. New text (the first clause is kept word for word — an existing case greps it):

Each ruling is one string naming the decision, the reason, and what it costs if
the default is wrong, in that order: `<decision>, because <reason>; wrong costs
<cost>`. Keep it short enough to survive the steering projection that carries
it. Rule on what you would otherwise have asked, and on nothing else: the small
choices your role makes all day are not rulings.

R8+R7 — lines 151-157, from "Announce before any other work" to "you never edit that file by hand." Two rules in one passage. R8: the announce-timing rule carried an exemption bolted onto the general rule ("before any other work — after only the branch steps your prompt names"), re-cut into two branches on an observable predicate (row 4, and the ban on patching a rule with an exemption). R7: the no-hand-edit rule is row 1 and carried neither price nor excuse. New text:

Where your prompt names branch steps, run those first and announce on the
branch they put you on. Where it names none, announce before any other work.
The announcement carries the increment id and the label your prompt gives you,
and lands on the branch your step commits to. `<base>` is the base directory of
the `agent-brief` skill, which your context names on its `Base directory for
this skill:` line; where no such line is there, find the helper with `find
"$HOME/.claude/plugins" -path '*agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs' | head -1`.
That helper is the only writer of `backlog.json`: never edit that file by hand
and never write it with anything else — not "the helper rejected my argument",
not "it is only one field": a state written by hand is one the next reader
cannot trust, and a run that cannot read its state back starts over from the
beginning.

Keep the `find` invocation byte for byte as it stands, including its quoting.

R9 — lines 203-204, under `## You do not hand over`. Failure class: row 1. Keep the heading exactly as it is. New text:

Never dispatch a subagent and never call the next agent in the chain — not
"one dispatch would finish this": a step your caller did not dispatch is a step
the run state never records, and the workflow runs it again over the top of
yours. You return, and your caller runs the next one.

== CRITERION 4: NO CONFLICT AROSE ==
No rule on this page needed a requirement changed to reach its winning form, so `questions` is empty and nothing is left standing under protest. The one rule where a re-cut would have narrowed what it permits — "Read a file whole only when you need it whole" — is left as it stands, with its reason in the verdict below; that is a verdict, not a conflict, because the bullet already carries the observable predicate in its first clause.

== THE VERDICT, RULE BY RULE ==
Every rule below was read against all four rows and against the ban on bolted-on exemptions. REWRITTEN entries name the change; the rest carry the reason no rewrite is needed.
1. Frontmatter description — unchanged: rewritten and pinned by the previous pass (the skill-lead, skill-occasion and skill-nosteps cases).

5. Retry four times, then report the failure — unchanged: row 4, both branches stated on an observable predicate (the push still fails).
6. The default branch moves only through a human-merged pull request — REWRITTEN (R2): row 1, now a prohibition carrying its price and the quoted excuse.
7. Read exactly the steps and fields your prompt names — REWRITTEN (R3): row 1, prohibition and quoted excuses added to the price it already carried.
8. The prompt, its steps and your page are everything you get; do not go looking — unchanged: row 4, the gap is routed to the material/decidable test, which decides both branches.
9. Paths are inferred; run `git log` yourself — unchanged: a fact and a recipe, no failure class in the table applies.
10. A prompt may narrow the issue to one increment — unchanged: row 4, both branches stated ("Where your prompt names no increment, the issue is the scope, whole").
11. Follow the branch steps before you change anything — unchanged: row 4, keyed to the prompt naming them.
12. Your page lists the narrowest tool set; a withheld tool is withheld on purpose — unchanged: a fact.
13. Glob bullet — unchanged: a recipe stating what to use it for.
14. Grep bullet (ask for the context around a hit) — unchanged: a recipe stating the output to ask for.
15. Read bullet (offset and limit; whole only when you need it whole) — unchanged: the observable predicate is already in the first clause (a hit named the lines); keying the second clause to that same predicate would narrow what the rule permits, and its failure is wasted context, not a wrong branch.
16. Prefer a dedicated tool over Bash when one fits — REWRITTEN (R4): row 4, the judgement call is now an observable predicate with both branches.
17. Send independent calls in one message — unchanged: a recipe carrying its price.
18. The closed command list — REWRITTEN (R5): its branches were already keyed to a predicate; row 1 added the price and the quoted excuses.
19. Report the command, what it covered and its exit code — unchanged: row 3, prose plus a worked example that shows all three elements, so an omission is visible against the example.
20. Say so if a run skipped or excluded anything — unchanged: row 4, keyed to an observable predicate.
21. The mutation standard — unchanged: a definition the role pages act on, not a behaviour rule of this page.
22. The material/decidable test — unchanged: row 4, an enumerated observable predicate.
23. Material goes in questions, decidable never does — unchanged: row 4, both branches stated.
24. The price of a parked run and of a wrong default — unchanged: this is the price row 1 asks for.
25. The shape of one ruling — REWRITTEN (R6): row 3, prose asking for three elements now carries the template that makes a missing one visible.
26. Rule on what you would otherwise have asked, and nothing else — unchanged: row 4, the predicate is stated and the negative branch named.
27. The step return is the whole channel; the substance goes in the fields — unchanged: row 2, the recipe is stated first and the bans only fence it.
28. The questions / rulings / summary bullets — unchanged: a schema of what each field holds.
29. You produce it once; the structured object is not a second copy — unchanged: row 2, the recipe (only the values the workflow steers on, named by its schema) is stated, with the price.
30. One instruction per sentence, imperative, each thing said once — unchanged: row 2, a recipe carrying its price.
31. The announce heredoc — unchanged: row 3, already a template with slots.
32. When to announce — REWRITTEN (R8): the only bolted-on exemption on the page, re-cut into two branches on an observable predicate.
33. Finding `<base>` — unchanged: row 4, both branches stated with an observable predicate (the line is there or it is not).
34. The helper is the only writer; no hand edits — REWRITTEN (R7): row 1, the bare prohibition now carries its price and the quoted excuses.
35. What announcing does; keep the prompt file — unchanged: a fact and a recipe.
36. The record heredoc, with the same id, label and prompt file — unchanged: row 3, already a template.
37. Why recording before returning matters — unchanged: the price of the rule above it.
38. backlog.json is the single source of truth; nothing in it is deleted — unchanged: facts.
39. Read it only where your prompt sends you, never whole — unchanged: a prohibition that already names its price and the addressed reads that replace the whole-file read.
40. A repeated step meets what its first run committed — unchanged: row 4, keyed to an observable predicate with the action for each branch.
41. You do not dispatch subagents or call the next agent — REWRITTEN (R9): row 1, now a prohibition with its price and the quoted excuse.
42. Check mode fires on a first line of CHECK MODE — unchanged: row 4, an observable predicate.
43. The check-mode bans, the four-item ordered report and "a check-mode run that produces work is a failed one" — unchanged: row 2, the recipe is present as an ordered four-item report, and the price is named.
44. "What this is not" — unchanged: a fence, not a rule.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. They are bash cases in the existing repository suite, and they are the whole of the new test surface for this increment.

FILE: /home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh (plain bash, no framework; `set -u`, `$root` resolved at the top, `ok "..."` and `no "..."` increment the counters, a final PASS/FAIL block exits 1 on any failure).
COMMAND THAT RUNS JUST THIS FILE: `bash test-repo.sh`
LEVEL: integration against the shipped page — every case reads the real file on disk, nothing is faked.

SUITE DOC: there is none for test-repo.sh, and none is to be written. The doc would have to live at the repository root as CLAUDE.md, and the case at "no CLAUDE.md at the repository root, so nothing here loads as inheritable project memory" turns red the moment that file exists. Take the conventions from the file itself instead: a section opens with `echo` then `echo "=== <lowercase claim>"`, each case carries a comment naming the criterion and the exact Break that turns it red, and a phrase that wraps across lines in a page is matched against a collapsed copy of that page (`tr '\n' ' ' | tr -s ' '`), the way `brief_collapsed` and `reviewer_collapsed` already do.

WHERE THE NEW SECTION GOES: immediately before the file's final `echo` / PASS-FAIL block, after `rm -rf "$desc_tmp"`. Open it with:

  echo
  echo "=== every rule in the shared brief is written in its winning form"

and define one collapsed copy of the page for the whole section, e.g. `brief_form="$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$root/skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md" | tr -s ' ')"`. Every marker below wraps across lines in the page, so every case must test `echo "$brief_form" | grep -q '<marker>'`, never a bare `grep` on the file. Markers contain straight double quotes; put them inside single-quoted shell strings so no escaping is needed. Do not reuse `brief_collapsed` from the distant "a decidable question gets a ruling" section — define the section's own variable.

NINE CASES, one per rewritten rule. Each states the production change that turns it red: restoring that rule to the wording it replaced.

Case 1 — the push rule carries its price and the excuses it counters.
Assert all three markers are present: `Never keep a commit local` ; `"one push at the end will do"` ; `an unpushed commit dies with the container`.
Break: restore "You commit your work where your page says to, and you push that commit straight away — an unpushed commit dies with the container that made it, and the run state it carries dies with it." The prohibition and both quoted excuses vanish and the first two markers fail.

Case 2 — the default branch is closed by a prohibition that names its price.
Assert: `Never push to the default branch` ; `"the work is done and the branch is green"` ; `a change no human approved`.
Break: restore "The default branch moves only through a pull request a human merges, and opening that pull request is your caller's, never yours." All three markers vanish.

Case 3 — reading outside your prompt is prohibited, with the excuse quoted.
Assert: `never read a step or a field it did not name` ; `"it is in the same file anyway"`.
Break: restore "and take nothing else out of them:". Both markers vanish.

Case 4 — the Bash rule is keyed to an observable predicate, not a judgement call.
Assert present: `use Bash where the thing needs a shell` ; `Use the tools above where one of them does the thing`.
Assert absent: `Prefer a dedicated tool` — this half is what catches the judgement call being bolted back on beside the new wording.
Break, either direction: restore "Prefer a dedicated tool over Bash when one fits — reserve Bash for shell-only operations." (the presence markers fail), or append that sentence to the new bullet (the absence assertion fails).

Case 5 — the closed command list carries its price and the excuses it counters.
Assert: `Never run a suite, a linter or a formatter the list does not name` ; `"the whole suite is right there"` ; `a failure someone else owns`.
Break: restore "run exactly those and nothing else — a suite, a linter or a formatter it does not name is not yours to run, however obvious it looks, and you never go looking for a runner yourself." All three markers vanish.

Case 6 — a ruling has a template, not three elements asked for in prose.
Assert: `wrong costs <cost>` (and, in the same case, `in that order`).
Break: restore "— short enough to survive the steering projection that carries it." directly after "...if the default is wrong", which deletes the template. Note for whoever writes this case: the older case asserting `one string naming the decision, the reason, and what it costs if the default is wrong` must stay green, because that clause is kept word for word in the rewrite — if it goes red, the rewrite broke a sentence it was told to keep.

Case 7 — hand-writing the run state is prohibited, with its price and the excuse.
Assert: `never write it with anything else` ; `"the helper rejected my argument"` ; `starts over from the beginning`.
Do NOT key this case on `never edit that file by hand` — the replaced wording contains that phrase too, so a case built on it stays green after a restore.
Break: restore "That helper is the only writer of `backlog.json`, so you never edit that file by hand." All three markers vanish.

Case 8 — the announce timing is two branches on a predicate, not an exemption bolted on.
Assert present: `Where your prompt names branch steps` ; `Where it names none`.
Assert absent: `after only the branch steps`.
Break, either direction: restore "Announce before any other work — after only the branch steps your prompt names, so the announcement lands on the branch your step commits to — with the increment id and the label your prompt gives you." (the presence markers fail and the absence assertion fails at once), or re-append the bolted clause beside the new branches (the absence assertion fails alone).

Case 9 — not dispatching is a prohibition that names its price.
Assert: `Never dispatch a subagent` ; `"one dispatch would finish this"` ; `the run state never records`.
Break: restore "You do not dispatch subagents and you do not call the next agent in the chain." All three markers vanish.

EDGES AND WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT TESTED.
- Empty and missing: no case needs a fixture — the page is a tracked file that always exists, and a missing or emptied page fails all nine cases at once.
- Repeat: none of the nine markers is a substring of another, and none appears anywhere else on the page, so no case can pass for the wrong reason. Whoever writes them should confirm that by eye against the rewritten page before calling it done.
- The criterion "every rule is read against all four rows and the exemption ban" gets no case: a reading is not observable in an artefact. It is discharged by the rule-by-rule verdict recorded in this research step, which covers all 44 rules on the page.
- The criterion "no rewrite changes what the rule requires" gets no case for the same reason: it is a judgement on two wordings, and the reviewer makes it from the diff.
- No case asserts the forbidden words stay off the page (occasion, rationalisation, exemption clause, chain depth, collector, handoff). The existing ownership cases already fail if any of them appears on a second page, and duplicating them here would be a second copy of a rule that drifts.

WHAT COUNTS AS DONE — the closed list, run from the repository root:
  bash test-repo.sh
  bash test.sh
Nothing else is run: there is no linter and no formatter in this repository, and test.sh already contains every suite.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED: I ran nothing, not even once and not as a baseline — a run buys no fact I could not state from reading. I know of no red case on this branch; the first run of the list above belongs to whoever runs it downstream, and a case that is red before any edit is a fact to report, not a failure of this plan.
rulings: The rule-by-rule verdict is recorded in this research step's `plan` field rather than in a new document, because the codemap names backlog.json as its home and forbids adding a document; if that is wrong the verdict has to be copied into a page later, which is one edit and loses nothing.

No suite doc is written for test-repo.sh, because the only place one could live is a CLAUDE.md at the repository root and an existing case in that same suite turns red the moment that file exists; if that is wrong the conventions stay where they are today — in the file's own comments — and cost the next test-author one read.

Six rules classified as skipped-under-pressure each get a short quoted excuse and a named price rather than a price alone, which adds about eight lines to a page every agent pays for; if that is wrong the excuses can be cut back to the price in one edit per rule, and the nine cases name exactly which lines to touch.
return.summary: Audited all 44 rules of the shared brief against the four-row form table and the ban on bolted-on exemptions: nine lose and are rewritten — six pressure rules gain a prohibition with its price and the excuse quoted, the Bash rule and the announce-timing rule are re-cut onto observable predicates (the timing rule was the page's only bolted-on exemption), and the ruling shape gains a template — with the rest carrying the reason they need none. Nine new bash cases in test-repo.sh each turn red when its rule is restored to the wording it replaced, and no rule needed its requirements changed, so nothing goes to the human.

steps.label: decompose

rulings: The page-by-page, rule-by-rule verdict is recorded in the run's step returns in backlog.json rather than in a new document shipped in the repository: every issue directory here holds only issue.md and backlog.json, and backlog.json is already the run's record. If wrong, the cost is one document assembled afterwards from returns that already carry the whole verdict.

The cut is by page group rather than by form-table row: an increment that audits one row across all eleven pages would touch every page five times and never leave the pages settled, while a page group lands each page finished once. If wrong, the cost is that a single form row is judged slightly differently across increments, correctable by a later sweep.

Each increment carries the issue's cross-cutting criteria scoped to its own pages, since every criterion is a standard applied per rule rather than a one-off deliverable. If wrong, the cost is repetitive criteria text, not missed work.

All five increments are depth full: a rewrite decides which form wins for each rule and each rewrite needs a new test that turns red on the old wording, so nothing here is already named down to the wording.
return.summary: Cut the pass into five increments by page group, the shared brief first because it is the densest and most load-bearing page and it settles how the audit is judged and how the verdict is recorded for the rest of the run: INC-01 skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md, INC-02 agents/planner.md and agents/reviewer.md, INC-03 the three remaining agent pages, INC-04 the argus, grill and retro skill pages, INC-05 skills/CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/agents.md. The issue's criteria are standards applied per rule rather than separate deliverables, so each of them lands in every increment scoped to that increment's pages: the read against the four form rows and the exemption ban, the rewrite that changes form and never requirement, the re-cut of an exemption clause onto an observable predicate, the conflict returned as a question where the winning form cannot preserve the requirement, the test-repo.sh case per rewritten rule, the rule-by-rule verdict with a reason for every rule left alone, and `bash test.sh` exiting 0. I rejected a cut by form-table row, which would touch all eleven pages five times over and leave none of them settled, and a cut of one increment per page, which would need eleven chains against a limit of eight. The codemap names the eleven pages in scope, test-repo.sh, and .claude/rules/authoring.md as the read-only standard.
